title: The Head Hunter
review: I always like it when intro credits make little nods to the work each person oversees. Like a flourish or shift in the music as the composer's name appears or a tasty sound alongside the sound designer's name. Here there's also a hand-written manuscript visible for the writer credit, coins for the producer, and a gross shrunken head for the director; It feels so intentional. This movie is about a man who lives an isolated life, and we get to watch his struggle told entirely physically and through facial acting, without dialogue. In that sense it's reminiscent of {Hagazussa: A Heathen's Curse} or {The Revenant}. It's {Perfect Days} except he's a witcher instead of a toilet cleaner.
